tariff_basics.title: Tariff details
tariff_basics.description:
Enter prices exactly as your retailer quotes them.

All times are AEST (UTC+10) with no daylight saving. This is NEM (National Electricity Market) time, the clock your meter data and network tariffs use. It is a pricing clock, not Home Assistant's own timezone.

data_description.effective_from: The first day these rates apply. Earlier days use the oldest rates you have entered.
data_description.prices_include_gst: Turn this off if your prices are quoted before GST; 10% is added to import charges.
data_description.supply_c_per_day: In cents per day, charged on every day.
data_description.discount_pct: A percentage taken off supply and usage charges. It never applies to export credit.

tariff_period_stats.title: Statistics per tariff period
tariff_period_stats.description:
Gives every import period its own kWh and cost statistics, so the Energy dashboard can draw each period as its own grid source in its own colour. Turning this on works out your whole stored history, which can take a minute. The combined statistics are not changed.

**To use them:**
1. In Settings > Dashboards > Energy, add one grid consumption source per period below. For each, pick its kWh statistic and, under cost, choose "Use an entity tracking the total costs" and pick the matching cost statistic.
2. Remove your combined grid source (or turn off its cost). Using it alongside these sources counts your energy and cost twice.
3. These costs leave out the daily supply charge. Enter the amount below as the "daily cost adjustment" on one grid source only, and leave the others at 0. Home Assistant keeps an adjustment for each grid source, and I believe it adds each one to every day shown, so entering it on more than one source would count it more than once. After setting it, check one day: the dashboard's grid cost should equal the period costs plus this amount.

The adjustment is a fixed number. It does not follow your tariff, so when the supply charge or discount changes you must update it yourself. It also applies to every day the dashboard shows, including days before these rates started.

{details}

Renaming or removing a period stops its statistics being written but leaves the old ones in place; clear them in Developer Tools > Statistics if you no longer want them. Turning this off keeps everything already written.
